Boyle, 47, first drew attention when she walked onstage for her “Britain’s Got Talent” audition in plain clothing and with an awkward demeanor, prompting laughter and eye-rolling from some in the audience. Moments later, she stunned them with a flawless performance of a song from “Les Miserables,” instantly becoming a sensation.

Boyle, an unemployed charity worker from Scotland who lives by herself with her cat, has inspired millions with a performance that challenges the pop world’s usual preference for carefully packaged young stars. By Friday evening, video of her audition had been watched more than 19 million times on YouTube.

The night before, Boyle had again performed “I Dreamed a Dream” by satellite on CNN’s “Anderson Cooper 360.” Speaking to Larry King, also via satellite, she said she had noticed the laughter her appearance caused at the audition.

“It didn’t bother me, because I knew I had to carry on with my performance,” Boyle said. “I didn’t know how people would react, so I just decided to give it a try.”

Morgan also admitted that he and others had laughed. “I feel as though I should apologize to Susan,” he said. “I’m sorry, because when you first came out, we didn’t show you nearly the level of respect we should have.”

“Then you came on, and honestly, we thought you were going to be something of a joke act,” Morgan said. “And then I remember the moment you started singing. I had never heard such a surprising and extraordinary voice come from someone so unexpected.”

For Boyle to win “Britain’s Got Talent”—a victory that would allow her to perform before Queen Elizabeth II—she still has to get through a live semifinal next month and, if successful, a final performance.

“At this point in the competition, she is the strongest favorite ‘Britain’s Got Talent’ has ever had,” Morgan said. “But Susan understands there are still two major obstacles ahead. In a live show, anything can happen.”
